title: Automated Knowledge Graph Completion
definition: The automatic generation and addition of relationships in a knowledge graph for new concepts to improve its density and connectivity.

difficulty_levels.beginner: Imagine a garden where every new plant is put in the right spot — it's not scattered randomly, but connected to other plants in a meaningful way. In the same way, automated knowledge graph completion puts new concepts in the right place in a knowledge graph, connecting them to related concepts.
difficulty_levels.intermediate: Automated knowledge graph completion involves adding edges (relationships) to new concepts in a knowledge graph. This is typically done after the concepts have been extracted and minted. The process can be integrated into the pipeline as an optional feature, triggered by a flag like --with-relationships.
difficulty_levels.expert: Automated knowledge graph completion is a key feature in building a robust and dynamic knowledge graph. It involves not only adding edges to new concepts, but also understanding the context and semantics of the concepts. This can be a challenging task, particularly in areas like natural language processing and machine learning. Automated knowledge graph completion can also be seen as a form of knowledge synthesis, where new insights are generated from existing knowledge. This has implications for fields like artificial intelligence and machine learning, where automated knowledge graph completion can be used to improve the performance of machine learning models.

extra_fields.insight: The harvester should automatically trigger relationship generation for the newly minted concepts to improve the density and connectivity of the knowledge graph.
